subject: index-shelf
notes: Stepped shelf, three folio stacks and open base remain distinct at 160x112, 80x56 and 64x45. Cream paper and green stone are separated. Larger foreground shelf reads well; no replacement for tactical tiles.

subject: reading-lectern
notes: Sloping blank folio leads; curved bracket and broad foot visibly support it. Clear silhouette at all reviewed sizes, with a useful open pocket under the stem.

subject: scroll-cradle
notes: Unequal scroll ends, hanging sheet and crescent stone support stay readable at compact size. Sparse spiral cuts remain subordinate; paper does not become a weapon or relic.

subject: floodgate-wheel
notes: Large open wheel against short masonry is distinct at compact size. Copper axle and attached support read; spokes become thin at 64x45, so keep as composition prop rather than tactical icon.

subject: broken-stair
notes: Broad risers, broken side face and one moss seam read at all reviewed sizes. Quiet plane construction; useful separable elevation prop.

subject: hinged-screen
notes: Unequal connected panels form an open V; hinge remains visible at native size. Compact reads as paired screens/windows rather than a doorway. Concept usage should preserve that reading.

subject: inkstone-basin
notes: Clear oblong lip, dark reflective pool and fitted low plinth. Pool is nearly opaque, consistent with ink; do not reuse this as transparent water or glass.

subject: survey-table
notes: Broad diagonal blank map and continuous heavy supports read clearly. Fine channel/weight details simplify at compact size, but map-table identity survives.

subject: bellows
notes: Connected boards, hinged handle, leather folds and tapered nozzle create a readable lateral gesture. Leather stays matte copper-brown against pale boards; identity holds at all three review sizes.

subject: quench-trough
notes: Long trough and steel bar read clearly with continuous support. The narrow water slit and steam become subtle at 64x45, so retain for scene compositions rather than a small water-status icon.

subject: anvil-block
notes: Long horn and broad heel sit on a fitted low masonry block. Cool iron and warm light planes are distinct; strongest single silhouette in this kit at compact size.

subject: clamp-bench
notes: Open vise jaws attach to a braced wood bench. Main mechanism remains recognizable at 80x56; screw details simplify at 64x45. This is a visual prop concept, not a mechanically validated machine design.

subject: crucible-stand
notes: Tilted ceramic bowl sits in a continuous two-sided iron support with a stable stone foot. Interior warm plane stays restrained; no unsupported molten splash or floating mount.

subject: coal-hopper
notes: Wedge body, coal mass and open feed door remain distinct at compact size. Fitted feet and hinge are clear; ember accent is subordinate to the structural silhouette.

subject: cooling-rack
notes: Open shelves, diagonal brace and two unequal ceramic molds remain clear at 160x112 and 80x56. Small slats simplify at 64x45; broad shelf gaps preserve identity.

subject: vent-chimney
notes: Bent hood, continuous flue and warm recessed slit distinguish the vent from the other props. Quiet stone base supports the hood; no excessive smoke or ornament.

subject: reed-bed
notes: Unequal curving reeds and low trough keep a clear contour at 160x112, 80x56 and 64x45. Waterline is subtle at smallest size; silhouette remains useful as a composition prop.

subject: root-arch
notes: One root grips the left jamb and curves across the crown; exposed right stone and broad opening read clearly. Copper-brown living root remains distinct from stone and moss.

subject: water-spout
notes: Connected ceramic pipe and continuous blue-green stream meet the basin. Thin water curve reads even compactly; water is a designed plane rather than transparent simulation.

subject: moss-bench
notes: Thick seat, unequal legs and left moss cap keep a grounded asymmetric silhouette. The quiet opening underneath remains clear at compact size.

subject: lily-cistern
notes: Broad rim, broken right edge, blue-green water and two unequal pads read at compact size. Simplified reflections distinguish the water from solid stone; no tactical-occupancy claim.

subject: vine-trellis
notes: Tilted support and diagonal vine remain connected. Open lattice and leaf clusters are readable at 80x56; leaf detail simplifies at 64x45 without losing trellis identity.

subject: seed-cabinet
notes: Unequal shelves, two terracotta trays and one climbing leaf read at 160x112 and 80x56. The cabinet is a scene prop, with no legible labels or invented contents.

subject: stepping-culvert
notes: Two uneven slabs sit visibly on stone banks above an open water channel. Broad span-and-void relationship survives at smallest study size; the precise traverse is not a gameplay assertion.

subject: beyond-tilted-observatory
notes: One large hollow copper-toned forged ring anchors to an asymmetric stone platform. Cream route, dark support void and quiet plum backdrop remain distinct at 160x112 and 80x56; distant floating mass is only a setting motif.

subject: beyond-silent-span
notes: A low S-shaped pale bridge joins unequal platforms, with visibly fitted end brackets. Route-versus-chasm remains clear compactly; the single sage cloth accent gives direction without obscuring the span.

subject: beyond-sealed-reservoir
notes: Broad opaque reservoir, narrow green inspection slit and short curved drain are distinct from a potion or relic. Blue-green water bowl reads at native size; the glass slit simplifies at compact size.

subject: threshold-rusted-lift
notes: Open empty cage, connected chain and adjacent landing read as a lift location. Thin chain links simplify at 64x45 but silhouette survives at 80x56. This is a source composition, with no validated lift mechanism or gameplay trigger.

subject: threshold-curtain-vault
notes: Three broad plum cloth folds hang from a fitted hook and partly reveal a dark opening. Thick stone jamb and cream floor wedge give clear depth; no visible inscription or invented vault contents.

subject: threshold-abandoned-bell
notes: Cracked bell, hanging ring, attached clapper and stone arch read clearly at compact size. Warm copper/bronze appearance departs from the prompt iron interpretation; retain that material difference for user review instead of claiming exact prompt conformity.

subject: exordium-split-ascent
notes: Pale rising stair leads around a dark outcrop to one warm opening. The incomplete right branch reads as broken traversal at 160x112 and 80x56. No route mechanics are implied; floating remnants are background composition.

subject: exordium-rain-camp
notes: Asymmetric copper cloth attaches to two supports below a broad overhang; runoff is separate from the small ember bed. Shelter silhouette remains readable compactly, with no character anatomy or clutter.

subject: exordium-sealed-door
notes: Heavy tilted door and warm lower wedge are clear against split rock. Copper latch remains subordinate; broad material planes survive compact view. Door fit and traversability are only visual concepts.

subject: city-suspended-market
notes: Readable suspended covered balcony with attached canopy and continuous beams. Market-specific shutters/stall cues are weak, so the scene does not yet establish the named market function. Retain as a useful covered-balcony source; semantic role needs user decision or later selective adaptation, not automatic adoption.

subject: city-aqueduct-crossing
notes: One pale diagonal route crosses a broad arch with visible stone thickness. Dark distant city masses stay quiet. Strong route-versus-void relationship survives at all reviewed sizes.

subject: city-rooftop-refuge
notes: Three broad steps lead into a dark sheltered pocket beneath sage cloth. Curved parapet distinguishes it from the cave camp, and the small warm lantern remains a focused accent at compact size.
